diagnostic_evidence.quote: Interestingly, the next lemma states that $c(T_n)$ can be diagonalized by $F_{\unitp,m}$ and its eigenvalues are the eigenvalues of 2-by-2 block matrices where their entries are the values evaluated at the partial sum of quaternion-valued generating functions.
for general $\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times 1}$, $F_{\unitp,m}\vectocirc{\mathbf{v}}F_{\unitp,m}^{*}$ has an $X$-shape sparse matrix

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims Strang's preconditioners are diagonalized by the DQFT matrix, in contrast to general quaternion circulants. What the paper establishes is only that the spectrum of $c(T_n)$ is a union of spectra of 2-by-2 blocks $G[f_m](2\pi s/n)$: conjugation by $F_{\unitp,n}$ leaves an X-shaped (block 2-by-2) matrix, not a diagonal one, and the eigenvalues are not Fourier transforms of the first column. General quaternion circulants are likewise only X-shaped under the DQFT, so under any reading the claimed contrast fails and 'diagonalized' overstates what is proved.

failure_location.quote: We show that Strang's circulant preconditioners can be diagionalized by discrete quaternion Fourier transform matrices whereas general quaternion circulant matrices cannot be diagonalized by them.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the abstract and the sentence preceding Lemma strangcireiglimitlm to state reduction to 2-by-2 blocks whose eigenvalues come from partial sums of the generating function.
issues.overall_effect: Misstates the nature of the main structural result for the preconditioner; no formal result is invalidated.
issues.title: Abstract overstates DQFT result as diagonalization of Strang preconditioners
issues.why_classification: A wording correction restores accuracy; all formal statements, rates and guarantees are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: With (1,2) entry $-\phi_2(f)(x)$ and (2,1) entry $\overline{\phi_2(f)(x)}$, $G[f](x)$ is Hermitian only if $\phi_2(f)(x)=0$, so the printed claim is false; the eigenvalues of this $G[f](x)$ are $(\phi_1(f)(x)+\phi_1(f)(-x)\pm\sqrt{(\phi_1(f)(x)-\phi_1(f)(-x))^2-4|\phi_2(f)(x)|^2})/2$, not $\check f,\hat f$, so the step $\lambda_{\min}(G[f](x))=\check f(x)$ in the proof of (ii) fails. The proof of (i) actually derives the quadratic form with the matrix carrying $+\phi_2(f)(x)$ in the (1,2) entry (the listed term 3 also has the wrong sign; correctly it is $+\frac{1}{2\pi}\int\phi_2(f)(x)\overline{\phi_1(\mathcal F(\mathbf y,x))}\,\overline{\phi_2(\mathcal F(\mathbf y,x))}dx$), and the final equality replacing this matrix by $G[f]$ is invalid. Counterexample: $f(x)=\sin(x)\mathbf q$ (a valid generating function: $\phi_1(f)=0$, $\phi_2(f)=\sin$ odd), $n=2$, so $t_1=\mathbf r/2$ and $T_2$ has $\bar t_1=-\mathbf r/2$; for $\mathbf y=(\mathbf r,1)^T$, $\mathbf y^*T_2\mathbf y=-1$, while the stated identity with $G[f]$ gives $0$ (with the $+$ matrix it gives $-1$). The proofs of (ii)-(iii), of tnhpdcorol, and of quatszegothm (which takes $G[f]$ as the symbol of $B_n$) rely on the false identity/eigenvalue identification.

failure_location.quote: It is clear that $G[f](x)$ is Hermitian for each $x$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine $G[f](x)$ with $+\phi_2(f)(x)$ in the (1,2) entry (equivalently $-\overline{\phi_2(f)(x)}$ in the (2,1) entry), which is Hermitian and is exactly the matrix derived in the proof of (i) after correcting the sign of term 3; then $\check f,\hat f$ are precisely its eigenvalues and the proofs of (ii), (iii), tnhpdcorol and quatszegothm go through verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The central quadratic-form identity (Theorem 2.2(i)) is false as printed, the Hermiticity and eigenvalue-identification claims are false, and the proofs of Theorem 2.2(ii)-(iii), Corollary tnhpdcorol, Theorem quatszegothm and Lemma strangcireiglimitlm (whose stated spectrum formula contains $G[f_m]$) are unreliable until the sign is repaired. The explicitly defined $\check f,\hat f$ and all downstream conclusions survive the repair.
issues.title: Sign error in the definition of G[f]: it is not Hermitian and the quadratic-form identity in Theorem 2.2(i) is false
issues.why_classification: The paper's central object is mis-defined, falsifying Theorem 2.2(i) as printed and corrupting several main proofs; the forced sign repair is contained and preserves every statement, rate and scope, so it is more than minor but not serious.

issues.failure_explanation: By stationarity $\mathcal{E}(x(t-s')\overline{x(t-s)})=\eta(s-s')$, i.e. $\overline{\eta(|s'-s|)}$ for $s'\geq s$ and $\eta(|s'-s|)$ for $s'<s$, the opposite of the displayed case split (for the MA(1) of Example ar2, $\mathcal{E}(x(t-2)\overline{x(t-1)})=4\delta^2\bar\beta=\overline{\eta(1)}$, not $\eta(1)$). Hence the system (linearsys) has coefficient matrix $\overline{T_n}$ (the conjugate of the displayed $T_n$) with unknown $\overline{\alpha}$ and right-hand side $(\overline{\eta(1)},...,\overline{\eta(n)})^T$; keeping the displayed $T_n$ the right-hand side must instead be $(\eta(1),...,\eta(n))^T$. As printed, $T_n\bm\alpha=\mathbf w$ with that matrix and that $\mathbf w$ represents neither pairing and does not follow from the normal equations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap the conjugations in the case split (so $[T_n]_{s',s}=\overline{\eta(|s'-s|)}$ for $s'\geq s$) and state the system as $\overline{T_n}\,\overline{\alpha}=\mathbf w$, or keep $T_n$ and replace $\mathbf w$ by $(\eta(1),...,\eta(n))^T$; the generating function (genf) then generates the displayed $T_n$ (or its reflection).
issues.overall_effect: The displayed system said to arise from quaternion linear prediction is not the normal-equation system; the spectral, HPD and preconditioning theory applies verbatim to the corrected (conjugated) system, so no downstream result is lost.
issues.title: Prediction system (hermqtsystem) inconsistent with the normal equations: conjugation pattern of T_n swapped
issues.why_classification: A local conjugation bookkeeping correction; all claims and guarantees apply unchanged to the corrected system.

issues.failure_explanation: For even $n$ the paper's Strang column places 0 in the middle position, so $c(T_n)$ contains only the coefficients $t_j$ with $|j|\leq n/2-1$ and the eigenvalues of the associated $\mathbb{Q}_{(0,1)}$ circulants are partial sums of order $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor=n/2-1$. The claimed identity $\sigma(c(T_n))=\bigcup_{s=0}^{m}\sigma(G[f_m](2\pi s/n))$ with $m=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ includes the extra pair $\eta(n/2)e^{\pm\unitp(n/2)x}$ and is false for even $n$ (e.g. $n=2$: $c(T_2)$ is built from $(t_0,0)$, so its spectrum involves only $t_0$, while $f_1$ contains $\eta(1)$). Part (ii) is unaffected since both truncations converge uniformly to $f$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $m=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ by $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ in part (i) (or define the Strang column for even $n$ to contain $t_{n/2}$ instead of 0).
issues.overall_effect: Part (i) of Lemma strangcireiglimitlm is incorrect for even $n$; part (ii) and all downstream convergence results are unaffected.
issues.title: Lemma strangcireiglimitlm(i): truncation index m=floor(n/2) is off by one for even n
issues.why_classification: A one-line index correction preserving the lemma's content, part (ii), and every downstream guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that $\sigma(\cdot)$ is right spectrum. Since $H_s$ is a Hermitian matrix, $\sigma(H_s)=\sigma(\bar{H}_s)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Since $\phi_2(t_k)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int\phi_2(f)(x)e^{+\unitp kx}dx$, the Strang circulant $c(-\phi_2(T_n))$ has eigenvalues $+\phi_2(f_m)(2\pi s/n)$, not $-\phi_2(f_m)(2\pi s/n)$; and since $\phi_1(f)$ is real but need not be even, $c(\overline{\phi_1(T_n)})$ has eigenvalues $\phi_1(f_m)(-2\pi s/n)$, not $\overline{\phi_1(f_m)(2\pi s/n)}$. The derived blocks $(\phi_1(f_m)(\theta_s), -\phi_2(f_m)(\theta_s); \overline{\phi_2(f_m)(\theta_s)}, \overline{\phi_1(f_m)(\theta_s)})$ are therefore wrong: with $\phi_1(f_m)$ real they have eigenvalues $\phi_1(f_m)(\theta_s)\pm\unitp|\phi_2(f_m)(\theta_s)|$, non-real whenever $\phi_2(f_m)(\theta_s)\neq0$, contradicting their similarity to the Hermitian $\mathcal M(c(T_n))$ (so '$H_s$ is a Hermitian matrix' is false), and the identification of the blocks with $G[f_m](2\pi s/n)$ fails. The correct blocks are $(\phi_1(f_m)(\theta_s), \phi_2(f_m)(\theta_s); \overline{\phi_2(f_m)(\theta_s)}, \phi_1(f_m)(-\theta_s))$; e.g. for $f(x)=\sin(x)\unitq$, $n=3$, $\sigma(c(T_3))=\{0,\pm\sqrt3/2\}$ is real while the paper's block formula yields the non-real $\pm\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\unitp$.

failure_location.quote: Their eigenvalues are given by $\phi_1(f_m) \left(\frac{2\pi s}{n}\right)$, $-\phi_2(f_m) \left(\frac{2\pi s}{n}\right)$, $\overline{\phi_2(f_m) \left(\frac{2\pi s}{n}\right)}$ and $\overline{\phi_1(f_m) \left(\frac{2\pi s}{n}\right)}$ ($s=0,1,...,n-1$) respectively,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the eigenvalues of $c(-\phi_2(T_n))$ and $c(\overline{\phi_1(T_n)})$ correctly as above, so the 2-by-2 blocks are the Hermitian matrices $(\phi_1(f_m)(\theta_s),\phi_2(f_m)(\theta_s);\overline{\phi_2(f_m)(\theta_s)},\phi_1(f_m)(-\theta_s))$ (equal to the sign-corrected $G[f_m](\theta_s)$), and redo the $s\leftrightarrow n-s$ pairing via the invariance of the eigenvalues under $\phi_1(f_m)(\theta)\leftrightarrow\phi_1(f_m)(-\theta)$, $\phi_2\to-\phi_2$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma strangcireiglimitlm (both parts, since the proof of (ii) invokes (i)) is invalid as written; the spectra-clustering theorem strangcircprecedmatspectrumthm and the superlinear-convergence theorem strangcircmainthm, whose proofs invoke this lemma, rest on it.
issues.title: Proof of Lemma strangcireiglimitlm derives wrong 2-by-2 blocks (wrong sign and wrong reflection)
issues.why_classification: The lemma's central derivation must be redone (a contained but nontrivial recomputation of the block eigenvalues and of the pairing argument); with this and the sign repair of $G$, all statements survive unchanged, so there is no major loss or new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for some positive integers $p,q$ such that $p+q\leq 4n_0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Each low-outlier factor satisfies $(1+\epsilon-\mu_s)/\mu_s\leq F:=(1+\epsilon-\mu_{\min})/\mu_{\min}$ with $\mu_{\min}=2\check f_{\min}/(3\hat f_{\max})$, but $\prod_{s=1}^{p}f_s\leq F^{4n_0}$ does not follow unless $F\geq1$ or $p=4n_0$: since $\mu_{\min}\leq2/3$, the regime $\mu_{\min}>(1+\epsilon)/2$ (i.e. $F<1$) is possible, and then with $p<4n_0$ one has $F^p>F^{4n_0}$ (for $p=0$ the claimed step reads $1\leq F^{4n_0}<1$). The displayed inequality is an invalid inference and the specific constant $C(\epsilon)=2F^{4n_0}$ is not established by this chain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound $\prod_{s=1}^{p}(1+\epsilon-\mu_s)/\mu_s\leq\max\{1,F\}^{4n_0}$ and adjust $C(\epsilon)$ accordingly (or keep $C=2F^{4n_0}$ and justify it via $F^{4n_0-p}\geq\epsilon^{4n_0-p-q}$, which holds because $F>\epsilon$ always).
issues.overall_effect: The final estimate in the proof of the superlinear-convergence theorem is unjustified as written; the theorem's statement (existence of $C(\epsilon)$) remains true.
issues.title: Invalid product bound in the proof of Theorem strangcircmainthm
issues.why_classification: A local estimate repair; the theorem's conclusion and convergence rate survive with at most a benign change of the constant.
